description: Rebuild a study plan after missed study days. Give each exam the hours you have already done and it takes those off the exam, then spreads the hours that are left over the days from start_date, using the same hours_per_day, hours_per_weekday and days_off as the plan tools. When an exam has topics, the hours done come off the topics in proportion to their hours. The answer shows the hours done and the hours left for each exam, and the repaired plan from start_date. Dates can be plain text, like Dec 12 or in 3 weeks. Example prompt: "I missed three days and did 4 hours of networking. Reschedule the rest of my study."

exams.description: Exams with name, date, optional hours needed, optional topics, and hours_done for the hours you already studied.

date.description: Date of the exam. Use 2026-12-12, or plain text like Dec 12, next Friday or in 3 weeks.

hours_done.description: Hours you already studied for this exam, in half hour steps like 2 or 1.5. Defaults to 0.

hours_needed.description: Study hours you want to put in. Defaults to 10.

topics.description: Topics of the exam with their own hours, so the plan can say which topic to study on each day.

hours_needed.description: Study hours for this topic. Leave it out to split the exam hours evenly over the topics.

name.description: Name of the topic inside the exam.

hours_per_day.description: Study hours available on a study day.

hours_per_weekday.description: Study hours for each weekday, like [{day: "mon", hours: 2}, {day: "sat", hours: 6}]. Weekdays you leave out use hours_per_day, a weekday with 0 hours is a day off, and days in days_off are always left out.

day.description: Weekday name, like mon, tue, sat or sunday.

hours.description: Study hours on that weekday. Use 0 for a day with no studying.

start_date.description: First day of the repaired plan. Defaults to today. Use 2026-12-12, or plain text like Dec 12, next Friday or in 3 weeks.

name: reschedule_missed_days
title: Reschedule missed days
